messages:
leah: thinking about the tradeoff between a small per-tenant 'bastion' proxy (L7 termination inside customer VPC) vs a mapping-only remote endpoint model (L4 passthrough + SNI-based routing). pros/cons?
aj: + bastion gives us fine-grained auth/observability, but empire of per-tenant infra and ENI count explodes.
sara: + mapping-only keeps CP simpler (no tenant-side proxy to manage) but makes certs & client auth harder. also harder to do request-level routing/fallbacks.
dan: what about hybrid: per-tenant lightweight L4 NAT proxy for IP preservation + central SNI-aware regional relay for L7 features?
leah: hybrid is interesting. main ops concerns: 1) scale of NAT allocations, 2) failover semantics when regional relay is down, 3) cert management when terminating at relay vs bastion.
aj: ops thought: if we keep termination at regional relay, cert scaling is big but manageable with wildcard + per-tenant SANs for top customers. smaller tenants: reuse shared cert and rely on client token for auth.
sara: the security bar for regulated customers requires end-to-end mTLS to tenant endpoint. bastion inside the VPC eases that since customer CA can trust it. mapping-only complicates proof of custody.
leah: question: can we preserve client source IPs for billing/abuse detection if we do L4 passthrough? mapping-only loses real source unless we do proxy-preserve header which is malformed for some ingress.
dan: we could do a short-lived IP-preservation tunnel from tenant ENIs to regional relay for latency-sensitive traffic. fallback to NAT path otherwise. adds complexity.
aj: also cost: per-tenant ENIs + NAT gateways -> $$$. We should quantify for 1000 tenants.
sara: proposal: define three customer tiers with clear contracts: 1) Managed Bastion (dedicated L7 inside VPC) for large/regulated; 2) Hybrid Relay (L4 preserve + optional L7 relay) for mid-market; 3) Mapping-only (L3/L4 passthrough) for small.
leah: +1 but need to specify failover SLOs and 0-trust handshake for each tier.
discussion: small notes:
- certs: Managed Bastion uses customer CA + our short-lived cert on the bastion. Hybrid Relay uses mTLS between bastion/relay. Mapping-only uses SNI and OAuth tokens.
- routing: prefer policy-based routing by tenant id header; if header absent fall back to SNI lookup.
- billing: tag per-path to attribute cost (bastion-hours, relay-egress-GB, nat-gw-hours).
- rollout: start with a few pilot customers on Managed Bastion to validate cert rotation and ops runbook.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: ``deploy/proxy-bastion/pilot`` queued for staging.
aj: next steps: 1) cost model for ENIs/NAT for 1k tenants (Sara), 2) runbook + failure mode doc for Managed Bastion (Leah), 3) small spike to test IP-preserve tunnel perf (Dan).
sara: I'll start cost calc, will post numbers by EOD Thu.
leah: I'll draft runbook and handshake API for bastion <-> control plane cert exchange.
dan: will spin up a perf spike (k8s job) to measure latency of short-lived tunnel vs NAT (aim for <10ms overhead).
leah: tagging decision: we prefer Hybrid Relay as our default for new mid-market customers; mapping-only remains opt-in for low-cost tier. Managed Bastion is enterprise-only opt-in.
sara: noted. also: need to update SDK docs about SNI vs tenant-header routing.
leah: good call. I'll create an RFC follow-up with clear interface definitions and rollout plan.
aj: thanks all. low-risk path with pilot -> iterate. :thumbsup:
